body: I stayed in Trincomalee for two days, and I loved Kanniya Hot Water Springs so much that I visited both days. Each time, the place was calm and peaceful with no big crowds, which made the experience even better.The seven hot water wells are truly unique — each one has a different temperature, and it feels special to pour water from each well. The water is clean, warm, and refreshing, and the whole area has a soothing, historic feel.The place is well maintained, and the environment is peaceful. The only small thing I was bothered about was the monkeys. They don’t harm anyone, but they can be a little naughty, so it’s better to keep your belongings close and avoid carrying food in your hands.Overall, Kanniya Hot Water Springs is a must-visit spot in Trincomalee. It’s the perfect place to relax, experience something unique, and enjoy a quiet moment with nature and culture.

body: Kanniya Hot Springs is a famous hot well in Sri Lanka from the past. There are seven wells in a square shape. Wells are only 3–4 feet deep and you can clearly see the bottom. The temperature is considerably high but vary from one spring to another.The pre-history of Kanniya Hot water spring goes back Ravana era and the first written references to the Hot water spring is found in the epic Ramayana. In the ancient time, there was a Buddhist temple complex in this site and the entrance is a part of a Buddhist monastery. Today this site is under the authority of Sri Lankan Archaeological department.I visited with my family, the water is crystal clear,and the water is sweet is taste. Even in that hot sun around you, a shower in this water is refreshing, but remember not to use soap or shampoo, and foot wear is not allowed, as its a religious place. The locals flock here to have a quick bath thinking the water has medicinal properties. It's probably a load of tripe.The place hasn't been looked after properly. There is no proper paved path to the wells--it's all sand, soil and rocks. Health and safety is non-existent. For example, there are a few step down which one has to descend to reach the wells. There are no safety rails to prevent people falling off these precarious stairs.There are also no sensible safe, dry and hygienic facilities for people to get changed. One wonders what they do with the money they collect--no investment at all. The locals would describe this lack of investment as "trying to fry snacks in water".

body: The entrance fee for locals who are able to read sinhalese and tamil is Rs.10 each whilst those able to only read english have to pay Rs.50 each. This is clearly mentioned in the large notice board hanging by the ticket office. Blatent Discrimination or Racism?? body: Kanniya Hot Spings is an interesting place and of historical value, particularly for the Hindus. There are 2 versions of stories doing the rounds; (1) Ravana created these 7 weeks to pay homage to his mother and (2) Hanuman created these wells for Seetha to cleanse herself before leaving Lanka either too hot or too cold for Seetha's liking until the 7th well was of the right temperature!However a loud Buddhist preaching or a message/song in Sinhalese plays in the background - do not know the buddhist connection to this place.There are a lot of local visitors, Hindus as well as Buddhists besides a small number of tourists who are charges 50 Lankan Rupees for entry.The wells have algae on the sides and the floors could be slippery but the water from the wells range from moderately hot to hot and clean with a slight hint of sulphurous smell. There are changing rooms by the sides but toilets are a bit farther away and not at all clean.This place could be developed further to make it tourist friendly. Visit this if you have a lot of (spare) time at Trincomalee and could be skipped.

body: I visited the hot spring many years ago and was horrified by the changes. The grounds are poorly maintained with trash strewn everywhere. The wells do not look particularly clean either, so our party did not go in. What was especially sad was that the wells have lost the spiritual, almost magical feel they had previously. The enormous military presence, like everywhere in the Trincomalee area certainly does not help. On our way to the wells, we were stopped at a check point. A soldier asked to ride with us to the wells. He might have been getting a ride quite simply. I certainly was not comfortable having an armed soldier in the same vehicle as my sleeping three-year old. But, you can hardly refuse when an armed man in uniform asks you for a ride, can you? The hot wells are full of soldiers too, ordering people around at the ticket counters and being generally very rude. Quite unpleasant.

title: Hot Springs
body: The springs are actually square wells holding the hot water at different temperatures ( all very hot) we were lucky to get in before a tour group of school boys who went a little crazy once they felt the water. It is very slippery so be careful as you remove your shoes before entering the enclosure. Worth a quick visit but if you have limited time it is something you can miss.

title: Too many people….
body: this place is a local attraction. you can see lot of local people and westerners here. There are 7 small ponds which is filled with hot water. It is said that these never go out of water. We say all the people taking bath here and it was crowded. There is a queue to avail the bucket and it also has an entrance fee of 50 Srilankan Rupee.

title: Natural Hot Water
body: It is surprising what the nature could do. There are couple of springs here and all have hot water and the hotness changes from well to well. It is comfortably warm but the problem is if you go during the day time, you will not be able to enjoy it much as there are so many people bathing here. I don't really approve of 'mass' bathing and wasting the resources. However, it can't be stopped. You need to take your own bucket there is a covered place for you to change clothes and you can look at Noora M's review for more details in this regard.Close to the springs, there is also an old temple which is said to have been built by a king. Some speculate that the hot wells may have been used by the kings during the days of the old. If you visit Trincomalee, this is a must see. Especially if you are not a Sri Lanka, I think you should visit this wonder of nature.

title: A real treat early morning
body: I am surprised Kanniya has only just made it on here. Its about 15 mins outside of Trinco. Its only 10 rupees or locals and 50 for tourists and you can bathe from the 7 hot springs. Get there for bang on 7am or soon after that the masses will arrive. take your own bucket if you can to scoop the water. There are changing facilities but these are very basic so bring a few towels to cover yourself with. You will feel great afterwards, especially if you have been feeling under the weather. A really beautiful place and a great start to the day.
